methods.steps: Open the TIF; choose File > Export, pick PNG in the Format menu, then click Save.
methods.limits: The Format menu lists PNG alongside HEIC, JPEG, JPEG-2000, OpenEXR, PDF and TIFF.

methods.steps: Open the scan, choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .png and click Export.
methods.limits: GIMP names the default file Untitled.png; you edit the name and extension in the Name field.

methods.steps: Run magick 'scan.tif[0]' scan.png.
methods.limits: A frame number in brackets picks one image from a multi-frame file, counting from zero; quote the name because shells interpret brackets.

methods.steps: Run dwebp input.webp -o input.png; in Inkscape choose File > Import, select the image with the Selector tool, then choose Path > Trace Bitmap, set the options and click OK.
methods.limits: Tracing is not a faithful copy, and color tracing makes one object per color; dwebp does not read animated WebP.

methods.steps: Run dwebp input.webp -bmp -o input.bmp, then potrace -s input.bmp -o output.svg.
methods.limits: Potrace reads PBM, PGM, PPM and BMP; dwebp does not read animated WebP.

methods.steps: Drag the ARW into the Input tab; on the Output tab choose the destination folder, JPEG as the target format and its quality settings, then click Convert.
methods.limits: XnView's format list names Sony RAW with the extension arw.

methods.steps: In the export module set target storage to file on disk, choose the file format, set the quality (default 95) and press Start export.
methods.limits: The export module's quality field defaults to 95.

methods.steps: Run magick input.arw output.jpg.
methods.limits: ImageMagick takes the output format from the file extension; its format list shows ARW as read-only and JPEG as read and write.

methods.steps: Open the picture, choose File > Export, pick JPEG in the Format menu, then click Save.
methods.limits: The quality slider appears for JPEG and JPEG-2000.

methods.steps: Open the file, choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .jpeg and click Export.
methods.limits: You edit the name and extension in the Name field.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jfif output.jpeg.
methods.limits: ImageMagick takes the output format from the file extension; its JPEG reader handles JFIF.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i book.m4b -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 192k -vn book.mp3.
methods.limits: Needs a build with the libmp3lame encoder; -vn disables automatic selection of any video stream.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mkv -c copy output.mov.
methods.limits: The special value copy means the stream is not re-encoded, so MOV must accept the copied codecs.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mkv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac output.mov.
methods.limits: FFmpeg transcodes every stream unless you specify -c copy, so this is slower than a copy.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp4 output.wmv.
methods.limits: FFmpeg chooses the default codecs for the output.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -c:v wmv2 -c:a wmav2 output.wmv.
methods.limits: Needs a build that includes the wmv2 and wmav2 encoders.

methods.steps: Use Media > Convert/Save, add the source, select Video - WMV + WMA (ASF), set a .wmv destination, then Start.
methods.limits: The profile uses WMV2 and WMA2.

methods.steps: Open the PNG, choose File > Export As, put .bmp at the end of the Name field and click Export.
methods.limits: You edit the name and extension in the Name field.

methods.steps: Run magick input.png output.bmp; use magick input.png BMP3:output.bmp only when version-three output is required.
methods.limits: BMP, BMP2 and BMP3 write different header versions; the default is version 4.

methods.steps: Drag the PNG into the Input tab; on the Output tab choose the destination folder and BMP as the format, then click Convert.
methods.limits: XnConvert's format list names BMP.

methods.steps: Run magick 'master.tiff[0]' copy.png.
methods.limits: A frame number in brackets picks one image from a multi-frame file, counting from zero; quote the name because shells interpret brackets.

methods.steps: Open the TIFF, choose File > Export As, type a name ending in .png and click Export.
methods.limits: You edit the name and extension in the Name field.

methods.steps: Open the TIFF, choose File > Export, pick PNG in the Format menu and click Save.
methods.limits: To convert several files at once, open them in one Preview window and select them in the sidebar.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.ts -c copy output.mp4.
methods.limits: Stream copy does not re-encode, and MP4 must be able to hold the copied streams.

methods.steps: Use Open Source, choose a preset, set the file name in Save As and the folder in To, then press Start.
methods.limits: HandBrake may switch an MP4's extension to M4V when AC3 pass-through, SRT subtitles or chapter markers are enabled; a preference turns that off.

methods.steps: Use Media > Convert/Save, add the TS, choose Video - H.264 + MP3 (MP4), set the destination and Start.
methods.limits: The profile's name says MP3 sound; its audio codec value is mpga.
